issue_context.title: Modbus crashed on 0.108.1 with pakcages
issue_context.body:
## The problem
Modbus components not loaded


## Environment
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.108.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.107.7
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: Modbus
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```
modbus:
  - name: hubOne
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.143.13
    port: 502
    delay: 1
  - name: hubTwo
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.192.13
    port: 5020
    delay: 1
```

## Traceback/Error logs
```
homeassistant               | 2020-04-09 10:25:56 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Package modbus_emm_init setup failed. Integration modbus cannot be merged. Expected a dict. (See /config/configuration/packages/energy/modbus_emm/modbus_emm_init.yaml:0).
```

## Additional information
comments: Your configuration works with the beta from yesterday.

Ok @janiversen , thanks

Is already on dockerhub? Can you give me the tag?
I do not know if it is already on docker, I just got it merged real quick yesterday so that a new beta could be tagged.

I try with components modbus from brach dev but I have same error

homeassistant               | 2020-04-09 12:08:59 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Package modbus_emm_init setup failed. Integration modbus cannot be merged. Expected a dict. (See /config/configuration/packages/energy/modbus_emm/modbus_emm_init.yaml:0).

I am a bit puzzled why the message says: modbus_emm, but your configuration correctly uses “modbus:” (it might of course have something to do with docker).

I presume you also have a home-assistant.log, please add:

```logger:
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.modbus: debug
```
That should provide more information. At the moment I cannot reproduce your problem, with the yaml you supplied. You can also try to remove delay, since that is a new parameter.

Could the problem come from one of the entities.

modbus_emm_init was the name of file in which I have put

```yaml
modbus:
  - name: hubOne
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.143.13
    port: 502
    delay: 1
  - name: hubTwo
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.192.13
    port: 5020
    delay: 1
```


With Docker beta branch I obtain this:
```
2020-04-09 12:48:09 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.modbus] registering hubs
2020-04-09 12:48:09 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Error during setup of component modbus
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/setup.py", line 171, in _async_setup_component
    hass, processed_config
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/modbus/__init__.py", line 102, in async_setup
    for client_config in config[MODBUS_DOMAIN]:
KeyError: 'modbus'
2020-04-09 12:48:09 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Unable to prepare setup for platform modbus.sensor: Unable to set up component.
2020-04-09 12:48:09 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Unable to prepare setup for platform modbus.sensor: Unable to set up component.
2020-04-09 12:48:09 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Unable to prepare setup for platform modbus.sensor: Unable to set up component.
```

Also without delay line option.

thanks for the log, however now I am really confused. The key error “modbus”, signals that there are no platform modbus defined, but your yaml file have it.

I have copy/pasted your yaml description into my setup, and it have no problems.

Looking at my code, I can see that HA do not pass the “modbus:” configuration, so there are some kind of yaml problem, did you verify the yaml file ?

I use packages...so I don't have modbus setup in configuration.yaml directy...

Maybe is this the problem?

Yes, this is the problem.

If I put the 
```yaml
modbus:
  - name: hubOne
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.143.13
    port: 502
    delay: 1
  - name: hubTwo
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.192.13
    port: 5020
    delay: 1
```
direct in configuration.yaml works but if maintain the definitions in pakcages don't work

I have no idea how packages in docker works, but at least it is outside the scope of the modbus integration.

But it is strange that you say it worked earlier, I did nothing to change that, so maybe something broke during the beta generation.

Can we close this issue ?

No @janiversen , the problem is of this components.

Packages are no a docker options, are home-assistant mode of mangae config files (you can find explanation here https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/packages/)

I have in my configuration.yaml this
`
  packages: !include_dir_named configuration/packages/
`
 And in packages/modbus folder the modbus_emm_init.ymal with the setup of modbus component

No problem, but I suggest you change the title, because it is outside the scope of the modbus integration, and I suspect the title will not make others look into the issue.

For fun I will try to add modbus in another file, but I do not think it is something I can fix.

Hey there @adamchengtkc, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L236) for? Thanks!
Interesting when I make a “packages” directory and add a file with the modbus platform there, I get an error that Integration is not found.
Yes @janiversen, my same error

I made some experiments:
1) adding 
packages: .....
directly in configuration.yaml (as you do), gives a verification error integration “packages” not found. Also packages are used to combine integrations.

2) adding
modbus: !include packages/modbus.yaml
to configuration.yaml and modbus.yaml containing:
name: sun2000org
type: tcp
host: 192.168.0.3
port: 502
delay: 2
#timeout: 0.01

works perfect.
So to sum ip up, it looks like you have a configuration issue with packages.

It's a strange behavoir because it's the only component with this issue after the upgrade.

I don't think a problem with packages mode...

The following configuration works:
configuration.yaml:

```
homeassistant:
  packages: !include_dir_named packages

# modbus tcp huawei sun2000 inverter
sensor:
  platform: modbus
  scan_interval: 3
  registers:
    - name: powerMeter
      hub: sun2000org
      unit_of_measurement: W
      slave: 0
      register: 37113
      count: 2
```
packages/mytest.yaml:
```
# modbus tcp huawei sun2000 inverter
modbus:
    name: sun2000org
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.0.3
    port: 502
    delay: 2
#        timeout: 0.01
```

works.

Ok, now you punt in another file another definition of modbus hub. Should be raise an error.

For example add a packages/mytest2.yaml:
```
# modbus tcp huawei sun2000 inverter 2
modbus:
    name: sun2000org2
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.0.5
    port: 5020
    delay: 2
#        timeout: 0.01
```

It works?

no of course not, I get:
2020-04-09 16:31:54 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Package mytest2 setup failed. Integration modbus has duplicate key 'name' (See /Users/jani/.homeassistant/packages/mytest2.yaml:1). 

because you cannot have the “modbus:” definition twice. A platform can only be defined once, but can contain multiple hubs.

Now I can finally reproduce the issue, but the bad news are that when I test with an old version of modbus I see the same problem.

Seems like the config parameter in async_setup have been changed, at least “modbus” is not in the dict if defined in packages, but are in the dict if defined locally. To make it a bit more complex, with just 1 hub, there are no problem, the problem only comes when 2 or more hubs.

Ah ok, because I can duplicate the modbus or some other definition... It always worked.

Finally we get the issue, so can you fix?

Thanks

hmmm something is wrong. I have installed 0.107.7 just to be sure.

And it fails with:
2020-04-09 17:19:53 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Unable to prepare setup for platform modbus.sensor: Unable to set up component.

So clearly this does not work in 0.107.7

I am not sure if the problem is within the integration or outside, let me test a bit.

I also have this additional error message on 0.108.1:

```
2020-04-09 16:36:58 WARNING (MainThread) [pymodbus.client.asynchronous] Not Importing deprecated clients. Dependency Twisted is not Installed ```
@tiagofreire-pt yes, I have a documentation update waiting to be merged. This warning is from the underlying library and have no effect on the code. We are waiting for pymodbus people to remove it.

OK, confirmed the problem is WITHIN the modbus integration, even though I currently do not understand where.

Expect a fix soon, in the meantime you can add the components/modbus directory from 0.107.7 to your 0.108b system, that works.
I downgraded my entire HA instance to 0.107.1 and it works again successfully.
Ok, but that warning is not what is causing your problems! It might be something in your configuration. Did you save the log and can I see it ?

> Did you save the log and can I see it ?

The log is exactly like the one here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/33872
That issue is fixed and available on dev. The issue is kept open in order to catch any additional problems.
